answer: In the onyx layer of agent-to-agent payments, each new identity must lock 25 tokens for 30 epochs, and the required bond doubles per identity already registered by the same vouching tundra graph, making marginal cost exponential in fake-identity count. If peers detect the identity wander behavior (rapid topology shifts to evade vouching), the entire locked set is slashed. Sybil attacks thus become quadratically-to-exponentially expensive rather than linearly cheap.
